question: At 1150 kg, what is the rotation speed (vR) for take-off with flaps T/O?
explanation: At 1150 kg, vR is 59 KIAS; at 1000 kg it is 55 KIAS, and at 850 kg it is 49 KIAS.

question: At 1150 kg, what is the best rate-of-climb speed (vY) with flaps T/O?
explanation: At 1150 kg vY is 66 KIAS; it reduces to 60 KIAS at 1000 kg and 54 KIAS at 850 kg.

question: At 1150 kg, what is the cruise climb speed with flaps UP?
explanation: Cruise climb at 1150 kg is flown at 73 KIAS, reducing to 68 KIAS at 1000 kg and 60 KIAS at 850 kg.

question: At 1150 kg, what is the normal landing approach speed with flaps LDG?
explanation: Normal landing approach speed at 1150 kg is 71 KIAS, reducing at lower masses to 63 KIAS (1000 kg) and 58 KIAS (850 kg).

question: What tire inflation pressure is specified for the main landing gear wheels during the pre-flight walk-around?
explanation: Main gear tires are checked to 2.5 bar (36 psi); the nose gear tire is inflated to a lower 2.0 bar (29 psi).

question: What tire inflation pressure is specified for the nose landing gear wheel during the pre-flight walk-around?
explanation: The nose wheel is checked to 2.0 bar (29 psi), lower than the 2.5 bar main gear pressure.

question: During the walk-around, when should the fuel cooler baffle on the stub wing be removed?

options.text: Only in winter operations regardless of OAT
Only if the Long Range Tank is installed
If the OAT on the ground is higher than 20 degrees C (68 degrees F)
If the OAT on the ground is lower than 20 degrees C (68 degrees F)

explanation: The baffle is removed when ground OAT is above 20 degrees C, to let cooling air reach the fuel cooler, and installed when OAT is below 20 degrees C.

question: During engine starting, for how many seconds at most should the starter motor be operated at a time?
explanation: The starter motor must not be operated for more than 10 seconds at a time, then allowed to cool for 20 seconds; after 6 attempts it must cool for half an hour.

question: After 6 unsuccessful attempts to start the engine, for how long must the starter motor be allowed to cool off?
explanation: After 6 start attempts the starter must cool for half an hour before further attempts.

question: During engine start, if the oil pressure has not moved out of the red range within how many seconds, must the ENGINE MASTER be switched OFF to investigate?
explanation: If oil pressure is still in the red range 3 seconds after starting, ENGINE MASTER must be set OFF and the problem investigated.

question: When starting a cold engine, oil pressure can briefly read as high as 6.5 bar for a maximum of how long?
explanation: A cold-engine start can show oil pressure as high as 6.5 bar for up to 20 seconds without being abnormal.

question: After starting, at what RPM is the engine warmed up until oil and coolant temperatures reach the green range?
explanation: After an initial 2 minutes at IDLE, warm-up continues at 1400 RPM until oil and coolant temperatures are in the green range.

question: Before taxiing, to what value should the idle RPM be checked?
explanation: Idle RPM is checked to 890 plus or minus 20 RPM before taxiing.

question: During the before take-off power check, between what values should RPM stabilize with the power lever at MAX?
explanation: At MAX power the before-takeoff check expects RPM to stabilize between 2240 and 2300 RPM, with LOAD stabilizing at 90 to 100 percent.

question: During the before take-off power check, between what values should the LOAD indication stabilize?
explanation: LOAD is expected to stabilize at 90 to 100 percent at MAX power; lower values are possible under high temperature and high altitude conditions.

question: During the before take-off power check, for how long is the power lever held at MAX before continuing the ECU test?
explanation: The power lever is set to MAX for 10 seconds as part of the before take-off checklist.

question: After lift-off, what is the airspeed for initial climb given in the normal take-off procedure?
explanation: The take-off checklist gives 66 KIAS for initial climb after nose wheel lift-off.

question: During the best rate-of-climb procedure, if oil or coolant temperature reaches the yellow range, by how much should airspeed be increased for better engine cooling?

options.text: 10 kts with no change in power
5 kts, with power reduced by 10 percent
10 kts, with power reduced by 5 percent
5 kts, with power reduced by 20 percent

explanation: If the yellow range is reached during climb, airspeed is increased by 5 kts and power reduced by 10 percent, accepting a reduced climb rate for better cooling.

question: What cruise power setting does the engine manufacturer recommend?
explanation: A cruise power setting of 70 percent is recommended by the engine manufacturer.

question: At what approximate rate does the electric fuel transfer pump move fuel from the AUX tank to the MAIN tank?
explanation: Normal transfer with the electric pump is approximately 60 US gal/h - much faster than the emergency valve's 18 to 21 US gal/h via the engine-driven pump.

question: During descent, above 5000 ft, what is the minimum power setting recommended to avoid unrecognized engine combustion stoppage?
explanation: Above 5000 ft, power should not be reduced below 30 percent; combustion may stop unrecognized at idle power above that altitude with outside air temperatures below -10 degrees C.

question: During landing approach, below what airspeed should flaps be selected to T/O?
explanation: Airspeed is reduced to 108 KIAS - vFE for the T/O flap setting - before selecting flaps T/O on approach.

question: During landing approach, below what airspeed should flaps be selected to LDG?
explanation: Airspeed is reduced further, to 91 KIAS - vFE for the LDG flap setting - before selecting flaps LDG.

question: During a go-around, what flap setting is selected once power is set to MAX?

options.text: Whichever was set before the go-around

explanation: The go-around checklist sets power to MAX, flies the mass-appropriate airspeed, and selects flaps T/O; above a safe height, airspeed is increased to 73 KIAS and flaps are raised to UP.

question: Before engine shut-down, for how long must the engine run at IDLE to avoid heat damage to the turbo charger?
explanation: The engine must run at least 2 minutes at IDLE before shut-down specifically to avoid heat damage to the turbo charger.

question: During the post-flight inspection, on what frequency is the ELT checked by listening for activation?
explanation: The ELT is checked as activated by listening on 121.5 MHz during the post-flight inspection.

question: Before refueling, what must be done to the airplane?

options.text: The parking brake must be released
The fuel cooler baffle must be removed
It must be connected to electrical ground at the unpainted areas on the steps
The ELECTRIC MASTER must be left ON throughout refueling

explanation: Before refueling the airplane must be connected to electrical ground, using the unpainted grounding points on the left and right steps.
